findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization Resource IDs, not group IDs, and evaluates the wrong resource
findings.body:
The method iterates over authorization resources of type "Groups" and (a) calls `hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), ...)` and (b) adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set.

Both are wrong:
- `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` resolves the resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Group resources are created with the *group id as their name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), so passing a Resource *id* never matches; the lookup returns null and the code silently falls back to the schema-wide "Groups" resource. Per-group `view-members`/`manage-members` permissions are therefore never detected here.
- The set returned is contractually a set of *group* ids (it is fed into `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ...)` in `UsersResource.searchForUser`/`BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser` and into `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`). Resource ids do not match any group, so the DB-level restriction matches no users at all.

In addition, `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` for the per-object resources it creates, so `resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups")` only returns the single schema-wide "Groups" resource and not the individual group resources at all.

Consequence: user listing/count restricted by group membership is broken under FGAP v2 – either no users are returned for admins whose only access is `view-members` on a group (when the attribute gets set with bogus ids) or the DB query is not restricted at all. The method should use `groupResource.getName()` (the group id) for both the permission check and the returned set, and the resources must be created with the proper type.

findings.title: canManage() grants manage access to admins that only have the 'view' scope on all groups
findings.body: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` (the no-argument variant) evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller merely has the `view` scope on the "Groups" resource type. `canManage()`/`requireManage()` is what guards `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup`, so an admin granted only a read-only all-groups `view` permission can create top-level groups. Only `AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE` should be accepted here (the `canView()` variant above already covers view/manage). Note the new Javadoc in `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` documents this behaviour, so the doc needs fixing too, and there is no test asserting that a view-only permission cannot create/modify groups.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the schema-wide 'Groups' resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In `hasPermission`, when no per-group resource is found the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`. That method returns `null` when the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false while the admin-permissions client still exists) or when the resource is simply absent from the store. The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and `resource.getScopes()` without a null check, which will throw a NullPointerException and surface as a 500 on ordinary admin endpoints (group listing, group update, user search). Add a null check and return `false`.

findings.title: getResourceName() does not resolve names for the new Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS`; for the newly added `Groups` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Group resources are created by `getOrCreateResource` with the group id as the resource *name* and no display name is ever set, so this returns `null` for every group-scoped permission. Any caller rendering permission resources (e.g. the admin console listing a scope permission's resources) will show `null`/empty instead of the group name or "All groups". A `GROUPS` branch analogous to the `USERS` one (resolving the group by id, returning "All groups" for the type resource) is needed.

findings.title: switch on resourceType throws NullPointerException for a null resource type
findings.body: The new `switch (resourceType)` dereferences `resourceType`, so a null resource type now produces a raw NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of the previous behaviour where `name` stayed null and the explicit `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object with type [...]")` was thrown. `getOrCreateResource` is reachable from policy/permission creation paths; guard against null (or use the existing validation message) to keep the error actionable.

findings.title: Javadoc of requireManageMembers() references the wrong method
findings.body: The Javadoc on `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` states it throws ForbiddenException if `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` returns false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers(GroupModel)` (a different scope: `manage-members` vs `manage-membership`). This is copy-pasted from the method above and will mislead implementers of the interface. Similarly, `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` documents "@return Stream of IDs" while it returns a `Set<String>`.

findings.title: Removal of the global-view short circuit causes a policy evaluation per (sub)group under FGAP v2
findings.body: `getSubGroups` previously hoisted `auth.groups().canView()` out of the stream and only fell back to the per-group check when the caller had no global view rights; the same change was made in `GroupsResource.getGroups`. `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` does not short-circuit on an all-groups permission, so for an admin whose access comes from an all-groups `view` permission every element now triggers a `findByName` lookup plus a full policy evaluation. For groups with many children (and for group listings) this multiplies the authorization evaluations by the number of groups on the page/stream. Consider caching the all-groups decision per request as before.
